about.title: Personal Injury Help in Trinidad, California
about.longDescription: Trinidad is a small coastal community, but its roads still see their share of collisions. Public records show US-101, Scenic Drive near 27 Scenic Drive, Patricks Point Drive, and Trinidad Frontage Road are among the corridors where crashes have been reported. In the most recent final year on record, Trinidad had 1 injury collision resulting in 1 person injured and no traffic deaths — a reminder that even a town this size isn't immune to the aftermath of a crash. Reports tend to cluster on Monday mornings between 9 and 11 a.m., which may reflect commute patterns along these routes. If you or someone you love has been hurt in a crash or other accident here, we can help. We are a personal injury law practice that handles cases for injured people in the area. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Understanding your options shouldn't add stress to an already difficult time — that's why an initial case review costs you nothing.

items.title: Contingency Fee Basis
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost. You only pay if there's a recovery on your behalf.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Allows Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In most ordinary injury cases in California, there's no limit on damages for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses.

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve your options.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews. Our team works on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: Yes. We are a personal injury law practice that handles cases for injured people in Trinidad and throughout Humboldt County.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California. If your claim involves a government entity, the window can be as short as six months, so it's wise not to wait.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to occur in Trinidad?
items.answer: Public records show collisions reported along corridors including US-101, Scenic Drive near the 27 Scenic Drive area, Patricks Point Drive, and Trinidad Frontage Road. These are simply the routes with the highest recorded collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still seek compensation even if you share some responsibility. Any award would typically be reduced by your percentage of fault, but partial fault does not bar you from recovering.
